_comment: Known engine bugs the suite currently trips. 'checks' maps fnmatch globs over check ids (<checkpoint>:<query id>:<aspect>) to a key in 'bugs'. Delete a bug and its globs when it is fixed. Some bugs only show up for certain segment layouts, so a listed check that passes is reported but only fails the run under --strict.

bugs.or-pruned-as-and: operator=or queries are segment-pruned with the AND term bloom, so a segment missing ANY query term is skipped and docs matching only some terms disappear (kosha-query search(): term_prune always uses TermBloomMode::And)
bugs.bm25-params-ignored: Per-request bm25_params are ignored: Bm25Scorer is built from the segment's stored params (reader.bm25_params()), not query.bm25_params, although the README advertises per-request k1/b
bugs.term-on-numeric-field: term/terms filters only consult string-typed fields, so a term on an Integer/Float field never matches (FilterApplier::apply_term reads store.string_fields only)
bugs.numeric-sort-lexicographic: Integer/Float fields sort as strings, so 10 sorts before 9 (build_sort_value_maps stringifies values; compare_candidate_sort_keys compares strings)
bugs.id-score-sort-uses-wand: Sorting by _id, or by _score asc, still takes the block-max WAND path (gated on sort_value_fields, which excludes _id/_score), so the page is the top-k BY SCORE re-sorted rather than the first k in the requested order; hidden on segments with tombstones
bugs.missing-posting-shard-503: S3 path only: a query term that hashes to a posting shard the segment never wrote (empty shards are skipped by the writer, common in small segments) is still requested from S3 during hydration; the 404 fails the whole search with 503 'segment hydration failed' (kosha-server posting_blob_files_for_query does not consult the segment's TOC). The listed checks are the ones seed 1 trips at the 10-doc segment written in the 'deletes' step (layout-dependent: the set shifted when delete-by-query started flushing buffered docs first)
bugs.delete-count-includes-tombstoned: delete-by-query's 'deleted' count includes docs that were already tombstoned (Indexer::delete_by_query counts every filter match in each segment)
